bull.b: Progress toward a confirmatory Phase III trial and a planned NDA submission creates a defined path toward potential commercialization. These milestones can improve the platform’s strategic value and provide important catalysts for validating Iopofosine I-131 over the next several quarters.

The reported response and durability data support meaningful clinical activity in a targeted patient population. If replicated in confirmatory development, this efficacy profile could strengthen the product’s differentiation and support adoption across additional hematologic malignancy settings.

Available liquidity supports planned Phase III initiation, ongoing development, and a potential NDA submission without an immediately stated funding gap. This gives management time to pursue value-defining milestones, although the runway remains tied to continued financing support.

bear.b: The absence of recurring revenue leaves the company dependent on clinical success and future financing rather than internally generated earnings. Persistent large losses also make it difficult to absorb development costs and demonstrate a sustainable commercial operating model.

Ongoing negative cash generation means operations continue to consume capital before any product revenue is established. Even with improved recent burn, reliance on external funding can create dilution risk and constrain development flexibility if milestones or financing conditions change.

A delayed European submission extends the timeline to potential regional commercialization and postpones the opportunity to generate broader regulatory and commercial validation. The delay also reflects pricing considerations that may complicate sequencing across major markets.
